```{r analysis}

max_gap_h <- 24  
all_states <- c("resting", "foraging", "migrating")
Shark_states_daily <- Full_Shark_Data %>%
  filter(latitude >= -90 & latitude <= 90 & longitude >= -180 & longitude <= 180) %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(datetime)) %>%
  group_by(id, date) %>%
  summarise(
    latitude = mean(latitude),
    longitude = mean(longitude),
    depth = mean(bathymetry, na.rm = TRUE),
    chlorophyll = mean(chlorophyll, na.rm = TRUE),
    sst = mean(sst, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  arrange(id, date) %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  mutate(
    next_lat = lead(latitude),
    next_lon = lead(longitude),
    next_date = lead(date),
    time_diff_days = as.numeric(difftime(next_date, date, units = "days")),
    dist_m = distHaversine(cbind(longitude, latitude), cbind(next_lon, next_lat)),
    speed_mpd = dist_m / time_diff_days,  # meters per day
    state = case_when(
      !is.na(speed_mpd) & speed_mpd < 500 ~ "resting",
      !is.na(speed_mpd) & speed_mpd < 5000 ~ "foraging",
      !is.na(speed_mpd) ~ "migrating",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    next_state = lead(state)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(state) & !is.na(next_state)) %>%
  ungroup()

complete_transitions <- expand.grid(state = all_states, next_state = all_states)

transition_counts <- Shark_states_daily %>%
  count(state, next_state) %>%
  right_join(complete_transitions, by = c("state", "next_state")) %>%
  mutate(n = ifelse(is.na(n), 0, n))

transition_prob <- transition_counts %>%
  group_by(state) %>%
  mutate(prob = n / sum(n)) %>%
  mutate(prob = ifelse(is.nan(prob), 0, prob)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(state, next_state, prob) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = next_state, values_from = prob)

mat <- as.matrix(transition_prob[, -1])
rownames(mat) <- transition_prob$state

row_sums <- rowSums(mat)
if (any(row_sums == 0)) {
  for (i in which(row_sums == 0)) {
    mat[i, i] <- 1
  }
}

mc <- new("markovchain", states = all_states, transitionMatrix = mat)
print("Transition Matrix:")
print(mc)

print("Example Simulation (10 steps from 'resting'):")
print(rmarkovchain(n = 10, object = mc, t0 = "resting"))

ggplot(Shark_states, aes(x = factor(state, levels = all_states))) +
  geom_bar(fill = "steelblue") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Frequency of Observed Shark States", x = "State", y = "Count")


mat_melt <- melt(mat)
ggplot(mat_melt, aes(Var1, Var2, fill = value)) +
  geom_tile(color = "black") +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(value, 2)), size = 5) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "dodgerblue", name = "Probability") +
  labs(title = "Shark State Transition Probabilities", x = "Current State", y = "Next State") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
  
  
```
```{r second}
# ===================================================================
# --- STEP 3: GRID THE OCEAN AND ASSIGN REWARDS (OPTIMIZED) ---
# ===================================================================

print("--- Step 3: Gridding the ocean and calculating rewards ---")

# --- OPTIMIZATION 1: Use a Coarser Grid ---
# A smaller cell size (like 0.1) creates a massive grid.
# Starting with a larger size (0.5) is much faster and often sufficient.
grid_cell_size <- 0.5 # CHANGED from 0.1 to 0.5 for speed

# --- OPTIMIZATION 2: Pre-compute and Save/Load the Slow Step ---
# We will save the result of the slow st_join() step so we only run it once.
assignment_file_path <- "shark_grid_assignment.rds"

if (file.exists(assignment_file_path)) {
  # If the file already exists, load it instantly. This is the fast path.
  print("Loading pre-computed grid assignment file...")
  shark_grid_assignment <- readRDS(assignment_file_path)
  
  # We also need the grid itself, let's regenerate it quickly
  shark_sf_daily <- st_as_sf(Shark_states_daily, coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326)
  ocean_grid <- st_make_grid(shark_sf_daily, cellsize = c(grid_cell_size, grid_cell_size)) %>%
    st_as_sf() %>%
    mutate(grid_id = 1:n())

} else {
  # If the file does NOT exist, run the slow computation. This is the one-time slow path.
  print("Pre-computed file not found. Running the slow spatial join (this may take a few minutes)...")
  
  # Convert your daily shark data to a spatial object (sf)
  shark_sf_daily <- st_as_sf(Shark_states_daily, coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326)

  # Create the spatial grid
  ocean_grid <- st_make_grid(shark_sf_daily, cellsize = c(grid_cell_size, grid_cell_size)) %>%
    st_as_sf() %>%
    mutate(grid_id = 1:n())

  # THIS IS THE SLOW LINE: Determine which grid cell each daily shark position falls into.
  shark_grid_assignment <- st_join(shark_sf_daily, ocean_grid, join = st_within)
  

  print("Saving the result to file for fast loading next time...")
  saveRDS(shark_grid_assignment, file = assignment_file_path)
}

Ocean_grid_rewards <- shark_grid_assignment %>%
  as_tibble() %>% 
  group_by(grid_id) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_chloro = mean(chlorophyll, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_SST = mean(sst, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_depth = mean(depth, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(mean_chloro) & !is.na(mean_SST)) %>%
  
 
  mutate(
    chloro_norm = (mean_chloro - min(mean_chloro)) / (max(mean_chloro) - min(mean_chloro)),
    sst_norm = 1 - abs(mean_SST - 16) / (max(mean_SST) - 16),

    reward = (0.6 * chloro_norm) + (0.4 * sst_norm)
  ) %>%
  right_join(ocean_grid, by = "grid_id") %>%
  st_as_sf() %>%
  filter(!is.na(reward))


print("--- Step 4: Building the reward-based movement model ---")

grid_neighbors <- st_touches(Ocean_grid_rewards, Ocean_grid_rewards)

transition_model <- list()
for (i in 1:nrow(Ocean_grid_rewards)) {
  current_cell_id <- Ocean_grid_rewards$grid_id[i]
  neighbor_indices <- grid_neighbors[[i]]
  
  # Proceed only if the cell has neighbors
  if (length(neighbor_indices) > 0) {
    neighbor_rewards <- Ocean_grid_rewards$reward[neighbor_indices]
    neighbor_ids <- Ocean_grid_rewards$grid_id[neighbor_indices]
    
    # Probability is proportional to the reward score
    total_reward <- sum(neighbor_rewards, na.rm = TRUE)
    if (total_reward > 0) {
      probs <- neighbor_rewards / total_reward
      transition_model[[current_cell_id]] <- tibble(
        from_grid = current_cell_id,
        to_grid = neighbor_ids,
        prob = probs
      )
    }
  }
}
# Combine the list into a single, efficient data frame
transition_model_df <- bind_rows(transition_model)


print("--- Step 5: Defining the prediction function ---")

predict_next_location <- function(start_lat, start_lon, model_df, grid_sf) {

  start_point <- st_as_sf(tibble(lon = start_lon, lat = start_lat), coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326)
  
  start_cell_index <- st_nearest_feature(start_point, grid_sf)
  start_cell_id <- grid_sf$grid_id[start_cell_index]
  
  possible_moves <- model_df %>% filter(from_grid == start_cell_id)
  
  if (nrow(possible_moves) == 0) {
    print("No valid moves from this location.")
    return(NULL) 
  }
  predicted_cell_id <- sample(possible_moves$to_grid, size = 1, prob = possible_moves$prob)
  
  predicted_cell_geom <- grid_sf %>% filter(grid_id == predicted_cell_id)
  
  return(predicted_cell_geom)
}
# ===================================================================
# --- STEP 6: VISUALIZATION (Corrected for Static Plot) ---
# ===================================================================
# Goal: Create a static map that visualizes the main components of
#       our model: the environmental reward grid and the historical
#       shark tracks colored by their behavioral state.
# -------------------------------------------------------------------

print("--- Step 6: Generating the final static visualization map ---")

# --- Create the Plot using ggplot ---
# This version removes the simulated click and prediction elements.
final_static_map <- ggplot() +
  # Layer 1: The reward grid (background)
  # This shows the environmental incentives for the sharks.
  geom_sf(data = Ocean_grid_rewards, aes(fill = reward), color = NA, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Cell Reward Score") +
  
  # Layer 2: The historical daily shark positions, colored by behavior
  # This shows the actual observed data on top of the environment.
  geom_sf(data = shark_sf_daily, aes(color = state), size = 2) +
  scale_color_manual(
    name = "Behavior (Rule-Based)",
    values = c("resting" = "orange", "foraging" = "green", "migrating" = "dodgerblue")
  ) +
  
  # Labels and theme
  labs(
    title = "Shark Movement Model Environment",
    subtitle = "Historical Daily Positions Over Environmental Reward Grid",
    x = "Longitude",
    y = "Latitude"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Print the final static map to the output
print(final_static_map)

print("--- Static analysis and plotting complete. ---")
```
